name: Wrist Fracture (Distal Radius Fracture)
seo_title: Wrist Fracture Treatment in North Palm Beach | First Rehab
seo_desc: Rehab after a wrist fracture cast or surgery in North Palm Beach. One-on-one hand therapy with a certified hand therapist. Medicare accepted. 561-624-4263.
lede: Once the cast comes off or your wrist is repaired, the work of regaining motion and strength begins. Our certified hand therapist guides each stage with your surgeon.
what_it_is: The radius is one of the two forearm bones and, near the wrist, the larger one on the thumb side. A break close to the wrist end of this bone is called a distal radius fracture. According to the AAOS, about 1 out of every 6 broken bones treated in the emergency room is a distal radius fracture, and the American Society of Hand Therapists notes the radius is the most commonly broken bone in the arm.

Most happen from a fall onto an outstretched hand. Younger people tend to break the wrist in high-energy accidents or sports, while older adults with osteoporosis can break it in a simple fall. Some fractures heal in a cast, and others need surgery with metal plates, screws, pins, or an external frame. Either way, the AAOS notes that wrist stiffness is common once immobilization ends.
symptoms: Pain, swelling, and bruising at the wrist after a fall
A wrist that looks bent or out of place
Stiffness in the wrist and fingers after the cast comes off
Weak grip once the cast or splint is removed
Lingering swelling in the hand and fingers
Numbness or tingling in the fingers
causes: Age over 60, when bone health becomes a bigger factor

how_therapy_helps.intro: After a distal radius fracture, therapy focuses on controlling swelling, restoring motion, and rebuilding strength once your doctor says the bone is ready. The American Society of Hand Therapists describes hand therapists working with the physician to decide when movement should begin, teaching swelling and pain control, and leading exercises for the fingers, wrist, and forearm. The AAOS notes that therapy usually starts within a few days to weeks after surgery, or right after the last cast comes off.
methods: The AAOS advises moving your fingers as soon as possible after casting or surgery. We teach exercises that keep the fingers, elbow, and shoulder from stiffening while the wrist is protected.
Elevation above heart level and ice, both recommended by the AAOS, help bring swelling down so the joints can move more easily.
When your surgeon or physician wants the wrist supported between exercise sessions, Laura Drumm, CHT, can fabricate a wrist splint in the clinic, a role ASHT describes for hand therapists.
Once you are cleared, we work on bending, straightening, and rotating the wrist and forearm, following your surgeon's protocol after plates or pins.
Grip and forearm strengthening is added as healing allows, along with practice on the daily tasks, work, or sports you need to get back to.

first_visit: Your first visit takes about an hour and includes evaluation and treatment. Laura reviews your fracture, how it was treated, and your surgeon's or physician's orders. She measures swelling, checks finger, wrist, and forearm motion, tests sensation, and assesses grip strength when it is safe to do so. She also watches for signs that need your doctor's attention, such as pain out of proportion to the injury, then starts your home program.
recovery: The AAOS says most distal radius fractures take about 3 months to heal enough for you to use the wrist for all activities. Light activities often resume 1 to 2 months after the cast comes off, and demanding sports 3 to 6 months after the injury. Full recovery can take up to a year, and some people have mild stiffness or aching for 2 years or longer. Cleveland Clinic notes full comfort and strength may take 6 to 12 months. Your timeline depends on the fracture, its treatment, and your bone health.
self_care: Keep your fingers moving through their full range many times a day unless your doctor tells you otherwise.
Elevate your hand above heart level to help reduce swelling.
Keep your cast dry and cover it with plastic when you shower.
If you are over 60, ask your doctor whether a bone health check makes sense for you.
see_a_doctor: Severe or worsening pain, a wrist that looks badly bent, or numb or pale fingers (AAOS)
Being unable to fully move your fingers within 24 hours of casting or surgery because of pain or swelling (AAOS)
New weakness bending the thumb or index finger, which the AAOS lists as a warning sign
Pain and swelling that keep getting worse instead of better, since the AAOS and Cleveland Clinic list complex regional pain syndrome as a possible complication

faqs.q: How long does it take to recover from a broken wrist?
faqs.a: According to the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons, most distal radius fractures take about 3 months to heal enough for all activities. Light activities often resume 1 to 2 months after the cast comes off, and sports like skiing or football 3 to 6 months after the injury. Full recovery can take up to a year, and timelines vary with the fracture type and treatment.

faqs.q: Why is my wrist so stiff after the cast comes off?
faqs.a: Weeks of immobilization leave the joints, tendons, and muscles stiff, and the AAOS notes that wrist stiffness is common after a distal radius fracture. The good news is that it usually improves in the month or two after the cast is removed. Regular motion exercises, swelling control, and gradual return to daily use all help. Severe or worsening stiffness should be checked by your doctor.

faqs.q: Do I need formal therapy after a wrist fracture, or can I do exercises at home?
faqs.a: Some people do well with a home program, and others need more guidance. The AAOS and ASSH clinical practice guideline found inconsistent evidence comparing supervised therapy with a home exercise program and says patient preference should play a large role. It also notes that some groups of patients may benefit from supervised hand therapy. Your surgeon and therapist can help you decide.

faqs.q: When does therapy start after wrist fracture surgery?
faqs.a: The AAOS reports that therapy after a distal radius fracture often begins within a few days to weeks after surgery, or right after the last cast is removed for nonsurgical cases. Finger motion usually starts right away. The exact timing for wrist motion and strengthening comes from your surgeon, and a hand therapist follows that protocol and keeps the surgeon updated.

faqs.q: Can a broken wrist cause carpal tunnel syndrome?
faqs.a: Yes, it can. Cleveland Clinic lists carpal tunnel syndrome among the possible complications of a wrist fracture, because swelling or bone changes near the wrist can press on the median nerve. Numbness or tingling in the thumb, index, middle, or ring finger after a fracture should be reported to your doctor. A hand therapist also checks sensation during rehab.

faqs.q: Will my wrist ever be the same after a distal radius fracture?
faqs.a: Many people return to their usual activities, but the AAOS notes that some have mild stiffness or aching for 2 years or longer, and in severe fractures some stiffness may be permanent, though it is usually mild. Cleveland Clinic adds that wrist arthritis is a possible later complication. Following your exercise program and staying in touch with your surgeon gives you the best chance of a good result.

signOrSymptom: wrist pain and bruising after a fall

notes_for_reviewer: ICD-10 S52.5 'Fracture of lower end of radius' verified on icd10data.com as a category. Billable codes need fracture type, laterality, and a 7th character for encounter (rehab visits typically use a subsequent encounter character such as D). Confirm with billing.

Honesty point: the AAOS/ASSH guideline (strength 'Limited') found inconsistent evidence that supervised therapy beats a home exercise program. The page discloses this in an FAQ. Clinician should be comfortable with that framing.

The seo_title uses 'Treatment' per the brief, but the page is about rehab after cast or surgery, not fracture care. Consider 'Wrist Fracture Rehab in North Palm Beach | First Rehab' if the site allows.
